enrol.question: How do I enrol my child in an Australian school from overseas?
enrol.answer: Start by shortlisting schools that fit your child's year level, location, and budget on SchoolGo. Each school's profile shows the documents, English test scores, and intake dates you'll need to apply. Once you've chosen a school, an education agent or the school's admissions office will guide you through the application and student visa process.

cost.question: How much does it cost to send my child to school in Australia?
cost.answer: International student tuition typically ranges from about A$15,000 to A$45,000 per year, depending on the school, year level, and sector. On top of tuition, plan for application fees, uniforms, technology, boarding (if applicable), and Overseas Student Health Cover. Every SchoolGo profile shows the school's published international fees so you can compare like-for-like.

englishTest.question: What English test does my child need for an Australian school?
englishTest.answer: Different schools accept different tests – the most common are AEAS, iDAT, Duolingo English Test, IELTS, and PTE Academic, with minimum scores that vary by year level. SchoolGo shows the exact tests and minimum scores each school accepts on its profile.

visa.question: Do international students need a visa to study at an Australian school?
visa.answer: Yes – full-fee international school students study on a Student visa (subclass 500), which requires a Confirmation of Enrolment from a CRICOS-registered school. You'll also need health cover (OSHC) for the duration of the visa. See our student visa guide for the full step-by-step.

agent.question: What is an education agent and do I need one?
agent.answer: Education agents are licensed consultants who help families choose schools, prepare documents, and manage the application and visa process. You don't have to use one, but most international families do – and it's free for you, since agents are paid by the schools. SchoolGo shows you which agents each school works with so you can pick someone with a proven track record.

schoolTypes.question: What types of schools are there in Australia?
schoolTypes.answer: Australian schools fall into three sectors – government (public), Catholic, and independent – and may be co-educational, single-sex, day-only, or boarding. Curricula include state certificates like the VCE, HSC, and QCE, plus the International Baccalaureate at many independent schools. Our school types guide explains how each sector works for international students.

free.question: Is SchoolGo free?
free.answer: Yes. SchoolGo is completely free for parents, education agents, and schools. There are no listing fees, application fees, or subscription costs.

find.question: How do education agents find Australian schools for international students?
find.answer: Agents typically build long-term relationships with a handful of schools and check each school's website, fees, and English requirements one at a time. SchoolGo replaces that workflow with a single searchable database of every CRICOS-registered school – filterable by fees, English tests, intakes, boarding, and scholarships.

englishTests.question: What English tests do Australian schools accept for international admissions?
englishTests.answer: Most Australian schools accept AEAS, with a growing number accepting iDAT, Duolingo English Test, IELTS, PTE Academic, Cambridge English, and TOEFL. Minimum scores vary by school and year level. SchoolGo lists the exact accepted tests and minimum scores on every school profile.

verifyScores.question: How do education agents verify student English test scores?
verifyScores.answer: Most test providers offer an official verification portal where agents and schools can confirm a score against the candidate's record. SchoolGo automates this – uploaded English scores are checked against the official record so you and the school know the result is genuine.

becomeAgent.question: How do I become an education agent for Australian schools?
becomeAgent.answer: There's no single licence to become an Australian education agent, but most schools and the AAERI/QEAC quality frameworks expect training in Australian education, ethical practice, and student welfare. The QEAC (Qualified Education Agent Counsellor) certification is the most widely recognised credential.

fees.question: Do education agents pay fees to use SchoolGo?
fees.answer: No. SchoolGo is free for every agent – no platform fees, no commission splits, no per-student charges. Your commercial relationship with schools stays direct.

manage.question: How do education agents manage multiple student applications at once?
manage.answer: SchoolGo gives you one student profile per family that maps to every school's requirements automatically – so you don't re-key passport numbers, transcripts, or English scores into 15 different forms. Documents are organised, version-controlled, and tracked for expiry, with every status change timestamped for audit.

attract.question: How do Australian schools attract more international students?
attract.answer: Schools grow their international cohort by being visible to families and agents in the markets they want to reach, and by making it easy to apply once a family is interested. SchoolGo lists every CRICOS-registered school in seven languages, with translated profiles, fees, and English requirements – so families and agents can find and shortlist your school directly.

verify.question: How do schools verify international students' English test scores?
verify.answer: Each English test provider (AEAS, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo, Cambridge, TOEFL) offers an official verification portal where schools can confirm a candidate's score against the original record. SchoolGo automates this – every English score on an application is checked against the official record before it lands in your inbox.

agents.question: [TODO: zh] How does SchoolGo work with education agents?
agents.answer: [TODO: zh] By default, your profile works with your school's existing agents. You can see which agents have placed students with you, invite new agents, or manage agent relationships from your dashboard.

documents.question: What documents do schools need for an international student application?
documents.answer: Standard documents include the student's passport, last two years of school reports, an English test result, proof of guardianship for younger students, and any additional medical or character documents your school requires. SchoolGo arrives applications complete – passports, transcripts, English scores, and required forms in one packaged record.

cost.question: How much does it cost to list on SchoolGo?
cost.answer: Nothing. SchoolGo is free for every school – no listing fees, no per-student fees, no commissions. Your profile auto-publishes from official government data, and claiming it unlocks full editing, applications, and analytics at no cost.

diversify.question: How do schools diversify their international student intake beyond China?
diversify.answer: Diversification starts with visibility in the markets you want to grow – Vietnam, Korea, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and beyond. SchoolGo translates your profile into seven languages and surfaces it to families and agents across the Asia-Pacific, so you can build a balanced cohort across multiple source countries.
